item.title: [LU-20173] sanity-sec test_31: unable to remount client (connection timed out)
item.description:

comments.comment: It seems this issue started occurring frequently after the landings on April 18th.

I think this is something environmental that is causing sanity-sec test_31 to fail with 'unable to remount client'. It started failing around 04/18, so I tried to bisect to find the patch that brought the regression, but now I can even reproduce when based on 2.16.0-ddn48, which had never shown any failure of this test at the time it was set (March 2026):
https://review.whamcloud.com/65678

yujian did you find anything on your side? I am continuing my investigations ATM.

"Sebastien Buisson <sbuisson@ddn.com>" uploaded a new patch: https://review.whamcloud.com/c/fs/lustre-release/+/65714
Subject: LU-20173 tests: filter on nettype when building nidlist
Project: fs/lustre-release
Branch: master
Current Patch Set: 1
Commit: 683ae43369bf82ac49fdcaa2b579b11a8c69b7e9

I think I managed to find the reason for these failures. sanity-sec test_31 adds a new LNet network ${NETTYPE}999 to exercise the '-o network' mount option, so it has to also add it to $MGSNID. But recently we started supporting Infiniband testing in Maloo, and it looks like the function h2name_or_ip to generate a NID list for a host is not designed to filter the addresses based on the nettype currently tested. This ends up using non-existing MGS NIDs, for instance <the ip over ib address>@tcp.

I have pushed a patch to improve h2name_or_ip and allow it to filter on the nettype being used:
https://review.whamcloud.com/65714
Let's see how it goes.

Jian Yu did you find anything on your side? I am continuing my investigations ATM.

Yes, sebastien. It's https://review.whamcloud.com/57780 ("LU-18637 obd: add 'network' server mount option") introducing the issue.

It's https://review.whamcloud.com/57780 ("LU-18637 obd: add 'network' server mount option") introducing the issue.

I do not think so. See the fix "LU-20173 tests: filter on nettype when building nidlist" at https://review.whamcloud.com/65714 .

Yes, the root cause is the change in our testing environment.
I mean the "unable to remount client" failure was introduced by that patch, because testing without that patch showed an error as "export for 10.240.25.41@tcp on MGS should not exist":
